font_ids: Retained R identifiers from user selections

items.lettering_notes: Keep Kristi's narrow sharp fast handwritten stroke skeleton. Make NIGHT the large visual anchor, in lively mixed-case handwritten "Night", tucked diagonally under a smaller "Where the"; "Goes" smaller beside the lower end, still read WHERE THE NIGHT GOES. Enlarge the first W into a tall open sweeping form that embraces the upper words. Elongate the N entry stroke and the g descender in Night into long confident cream strokes crossing the negative space between rows, with one thin return arc flowing toward the road reflections at the bottom. A very sparse rust-orange offset pen echo on just a few extended strokes picks up the lamp color. Cream main ink with imperfect pen pressure and sharp tapered ends. Preserve the shelter, bench and amber lamp completely. The lettering should be about 1.5 times the original title's visual presence, left and center; stay clear of the bench.

Retain Oooh Baby's fine near-monoline casual handwriting, airy open loops and round pressure-light terminals. Do NOT turn it into heavy brush script. Design a giant slender terracotta A at far left about 70 percent of the frame height. Its long diagonal and looping crossbar loosely embrace the remaining title, with "Letter" placed high beside it, tiny "to" nested below, and larger flowing "Spring" lower and slightly right. Spring's g descender sweeps under the composition as a long looping pen vine; 3 or 4 very small sage leaf-shaped ink strokes grow directly from this same terminal. The ornament and letters remain visibly hand-drawn flat ink, not photographic new plants. Terracotta title, just a few sage secondary hairline loops. Shift letter sizes and baselines dramatically but keep the title legible and bicycle/window/wisteria untouched. Boldness through scale, asymmetry and wildly long fine lines rather than stroke weight.

Keep Kaushan Script's forceful tilted broad-nib script forms. Make "Light" the dominant word across the middle left, roughly twice its original size, rendered in confident hand-painted DOUBLE-CONTOUR gold outlines with dark photo visible inside most wide strokes; small uneven filled gold patches at some joins reveal brush pressure. Exaggerate the opening L into a tall looping structure; extend the horizontal sweep of the t across one upper gap like a shaft of light. Set solid pale-gold "Leave the" smaller above and solid warm-gold "On" tucked beneath the right half of Light, with a very open looped O. One thin gold return curve from the L crosses the bottom negative space; avoid a conventional straight underline. Maintain lettering/photo contrast and the underlying dark wall texture within the hollow letters. Preserve lamp, chair, cup, tabletop and window.

Retain Rock Salt's jagged angular scratched uppercase monoline handwritten identity, NOT elegant connected cursive and NOT thick brush lettering. Put smaller "MEET ME" on a rising upper line, tiny "AFTER THE" nested in the open gap, then huge angular "RAIN" across the left-middle water. The tall R starts with a long broken vertical; its lower diagonal continues as a curling waterline beneath the rest. Use 2 or 3 separated parallel scratched mint strokes only on this continuation and the extended N ending, like ripples. The dot of the I can be an elongated ink droplet, still unmistakably an I. Pale-mint main letters and one extremely thin muted coral misregistered edge on a few strokes. Distinct uneven letter heights, strongly enlarged R and N, ample letter counters. Decoration connects to letter terminals and the lake horizon, never standalone umbrellas or rain clipart. Keep boat, red umbrella, jetty and mooring posts visible.

Keep the original Permanent Marker thick chisel-marker skeleton and confident blunt irregular forms, with hand-cut edge nicks and some quick dry ink gaps. Put small slanted "NO PLANS" along the upper left, very small "for" in a purposeful gap, then massive staggered "SUNDAY" spanning the lower left into the middle, climbing slightly. Make the S and Y unusually large and let middle letters tuck into their contours. Use hot orange SUNDAY, ivory smaller words, and one irregular yellow-ochre paint band partially behind just the middle of the large word, letting green show through. The Y exit stroke becomes a broad angular arrow-like gesture that tapers toward the open coast at center right. A few parallel chisel scratches and one small double underline attached to letters, all same material; no scattered icon stickers. No actual arrow text. Keep van, coast and doorway intact and readable. Broad graphic gestures, absolutely no stenciled neat look.

Keep Zeyada's thin whimsical upright pen handwriting, wavering almost uniform thin line; absolutely no heavy brush calligraphy. Design an extra-large open G in "Garden", its counter as tall as two small lines. Nest small "Let the" just above and partly inside the upper opening, then let the rest of Garden run right with playful uneven heights; put larger "Wait" diagonally below, its final t ascender reaching upward into the gap. A single long green pen stroke from the G curves around the title as an incomplete asymmetric botanical arch. Exactly four small flat ink leaves and one tiny ochre bud grow from that same curve; no separate sticker icons and no symmetrical floral frame. Forest-green letters with the smallest terracotta echo marks on 2 terminals. Strong letter scale contrast and airy negative spaces, visibly hand-drawn on the cream wall. Preserve wicker chair, side table and potted flowers.

Keep Amatic SC's extremely tall narrow uneven hand-printed capitals and thin spindly stems. Set small forest-green "BEFORE THE" high at left. Place enormous narrow "FOG" beneath it, reversed as unpainted pale photographic fog in a rough irregular burnt-ochre paint swath. The swath has only 3 or 4 broad uneven horizontal bristle passes and broken outer margins, confined to the left half, not a neat rectangle. Letters must remain narrow and tall, open counters. Below it, "LIFTS" returns as tall dark-green ink letters on fog, some letters starting higher; let the final S terminal rise as a single open green contour toward the real path. The O in FOG has a stretched irregular inner aperture that echoes a route contour, with one short thin outline continuation beyond the paint edge. Visual impact through negative space and giant condensed letters. No added mountain drawings or navigation icons. Keep bridge, path and forest on right unobscured.

Retain Water Brush's naturally connected dry-brush script skeleton but custom-compose the words in uneven nested groups. Small cream "The Last" high on left; large golden "Warm" beneath, and very large cream-gold "Window" along the lower left. Make the W of Window dramatically oversized and looped so the upper curl tucks behind the Warm line. Selected W and w sweeps have clearly separated parallel bristle strokes, 3–5 fine strands bending together with the curve, sea-blue visible through them; keep ordinary letter stems readable and largely intact. The final w extends as a confident long dry-gold flourish following the sea horizon toward the warm window, stopping before the cottage. One few-strand upward curl links the two dominant words. Bold contrast in word scale and stroke texture, no generic bar underline, no star or cloud icons. Preserve sea, cottage, window, roof and dusk lighting.

Keep Finger Paint's chunky friendly irregular hand-painted print letters, open counters and blunt notched ends, NOT thin cursive. Small warm-ivory "Take the" high left; enormous playful "SLOW" staggered across the center left; "Road" below with a large rounded R. Build SLOW in alternating restrained cream, burnt-orange and mustard letter colors, each letter a different width and slightly rotated with hand-painted rough edges. Add thin loose dark-teal and coral offset hand-drawn contour echoes to only selected letter edges, deliberately not perfectly registered, like the reference's color-play lettering. A cream finishing stroke attached to the d of Road bends outward following the real winding road, not an isolated arrow. A short mustard scribble grows from one W end. Allow a few natural paint flecks immediately adjacent to strokes, not a confetti overlay. Strong visual mass and irregular interlocking outline; keep the tree and vanishing road at right readable.

Keep Ephesis's fine elegant high-contrast calligraphic skeleton and graceful loops, not heavy dry-brush lettering. Make an oversized slate-blue N for Nothing rising almost the whole title block height at far left, opening into a long top arc. Flow "Nothing" across the top; small "Has to" in the interline space, then a larger "Happen" below shifted right. Extend the g descender and final n terminal into two asymmetrical extremely long fine tidal loops that embrace the words, open on the right; one ends on the real waterline. A single very pale translucent apricot broad ink wash sits behind a small central part of the title, with most of the sea visible, not a rectangular banner. Add a restrained fine pearl-colored echo on one dark loop only. Ornament through sweeping pen-line geometry, no shells, hearts, stars or separate badges, no symmetrical wedding frame. Strong scale changes but all words readable. Preserve empty sea, bench, closed umbrella and soft horizon.

Fine forward-leaning Bad Script pen forms. Huge C in City embraces small The; Fell Quiet sits lower and farther right. Stretch the Q tail into two delicate cream tram-wire arcs with one rusty-orange echo. Keep long strokes thin and sharp; no heavy brush. Dominant title left and middle, shelter clear.

Use Marck Script's rounded connected handwritten skeleton, open counters. Oversized M in Map occupies two levels, A smaller above and of tucked into a gap; Small Joys flows diagonally beneath. Terracotta and deep sage ink. A long p descender makes a folded open pen-route that loops under Joys; no separate map icon. Light pressure changes and expressive uneven baseline.

Retain Caveat's loose everyday tall handwriting. Place title on RIGHT, very large Blue Hour below small Back Before. Make the B twice normal size and open a long curving H crossbar. Cream main ink; just the big B and H have a second loose pale-coral contour offset a few millimeters, intermittent chalk-like edges. Rest remains simple pen; avoid ornate formal calligraphy.

Keep Covered By Your Grace narrow elongated irregular quick-pen forms. Title on RIGHT: The House small high, Beyond mid, huge August low with tall A and t. Forest-green fine strokes and one muted ochre wash behind the lower word. Extend t upward into a dry grass-like pen stem that is still part of t; a pair of short leaf strokes only. Deliberate unequal heights, roomy counters.

Use Gloria Hallelujah's bouncy handwritten print, uneven thick-and-thin monoline, not brush script. Giant looping F in Fireflies and a tall W frame the nested small Kept the. Pale yellow and cream alternating key words. A few tiny pinpricks sit on i dots and the F terminal like firefly light, with one incomplete looping pen track. No star stickers or scattered confetti. Large readable lettering in dark LEFT sky.

Use Gochi Hand's chunky compact rounded hand-print with soft blunt turns. Title on RIGHT: Coffee large, Before tiny in the middle, Courage very large offset below. Golden-ochre main letters, cream secondary words, a short uneven burnt-orange paint wedge tucked behind one C. Enlarge both C bowls; their finishing arcs turn into two short steam-like curls linked to letters. Not cursive; strong rounded open counters and playful tilted blocks.

Use Mansalva's spontaneous off-kilter handwritten forms and awkward angles. TOMORROW huge along an irregular rising line, Can small beneath and WAIT large shifted right. Butter-cream ink with restrained lilac and coral short edge echoes. Two letter terminals form a loose clothesline-like arc; a few short uneven hatch strokes where letters touch it. Preserve wonky pen skeleton rather than generic brush; no standalone clothespin icons. Title left-middle.

Use Satisfy's smooth soft brush-script skeleton, medium weight with clear pressure contrast. Title RIGHT: oversized S in Somewhere, smaller Between tucked inside its lower sweep, Trains large low. Warm ivory and lamp-gold. Extend the final s into two long thin parallel return strokes suggesting rails without drawing a train icon. Strong differences in scale, asymmetric loops; keep clock and actual rails clear.

Use Mr Dafoe's dramatic sharply slanted calligraphic brush forms. Small When the above; Ocean huge with a dominant open O and Answers staggered below, big A. Warm-ivory main ink and pale-seafoam strand echoes. O and final s release long fast dry-brush strokes in two wave-like directions; ordinary letters stay readable and connected. One ochre accent at an A edge, no separate nautical icons. Large title LEFT.

Use Sedgwick Ave Display's angular streetwise narrow graffiti letter skeleton with jagged broken strokes, NOT generic fat paint. Last Stop smaller on a tilted upper line; Anywhere dominates below with a giant A and stretched final e. Acid orange and ivory with a thin petrol-blue offset edge. The y tail cuts diagonally through a deliberate gap and finishes as a tapered route gesture. Sparse chisel scratches, no tag logos. Main title LEFT, garage untouched.

Just Another Hand's very tall slender compressed quick-pen letters; keep them narrow. Huge H in Home anchors the lower left; smaller The Long high and Way nested beside H. Ivory title with one rough moss-green negative-space band behind Home. One H downstroke extends into a thin crooked route-like curve following the track. Broken green contour echo on only two stems.

Sue Ellen Francisco's narrow long upright handwritten forms, slender and airy. Title RIGHT: Everything small above a huge Left, Unsaid tall beside and below it. Pale coral and cream with long L and U stems; a broad rough burgundy vertical paint fragment behind only Left, like a torn hand-painted poster edge. Uneven tops, a single long d terminal bent inward. No fake subtitle or film credits.

Shadows Into Light's thin upright handwritten print with angular open forms. Title RIGHT: oversized open S at the start of Still and Somehow, small Here nested between them. Deep midnight-blue single pen lines with a pale blue secondary contour around only the two S strokes, keeping interiors clear like cold air. A long w exit bends into a low broken snow-line; no snowflake icons. Strong scale asymmetry, never thick brush script.

Kalam's round energetic marker handwriting, retain soft blunt bends. Paper Boats large upper left, tiny in in the line gap, September bigger and offset lower. Warm ivory with rusty orange accents. The B belly and the S terminal are exaggerated; two attached angular folds in those strokes echo paper folds without drawing extra boats. One narrow broken ochre fill inside a big stem, relaxed irregular baseline.

Smooch's weighty, strongly forward-slanted connected brush script, dramatic thin upstrokes and thick rounded downstrokes. Huge K leans across two levels, Kiss the small high, Summer medium and Goodbye dominant below. Cream and deep coral. A long y descender crosses an open interline gap and returns as a sharp sweeping ribbon; tiny offset cream bristle echoes only at K and y. No lip or heart icons. Title LEFT, wheel clear.

Architects Daughter's angular architectural handwritten print, flat turns and consistent pen. Title RIGHT: Built small, from tiny tucked below, Sunday dominant and Afternoons broad lower line. Deep indigo pencil-like ink; selected S and A stems are double contours with exposed wall inside, a few short construction ticks attach to the crossbars. Long A diagonal relates to the chair leg. Clear sentence order; no measurements, numbers or detached blueprint graphics.

Annie Use Your Telescope's narrow lightly irregular quick handwritten print. RIGHT title with huge B and tall S, Under a small tucked high, Borrowed mid and Sky very large low. Thin ivory ink and muted gold accents; K diagonal and y descender continue into one open elliptical star-track line, three tiny dots placed along this actual letter extension. No astronomy clipart, no large moon, no cursive conversion. Preserve skinny letter identity.

Waiting for the Sunrise's extremely light tall hand-print and long upright strokes, not formal calligraphy. RIGHT title: very tall U in Until, small the nested in its open space; Birds Wake bigger staggered below. Dusty coral ink with one pale plum echo line. The B spine and final e exit extend into an airy incomplete sunrise arc, very thin and open. Long verticals and tiny round counters remain readable; no separate bird drawings.

Patrick Hand's rounded straightforward pen-print, readable compact forms. Giant N in Noise, A Little small upper left, Less tucked mid, Noise broad lower. Butter-cream and muted coral alternating only main words. O counter gets two loose inset pen rings; its terminal sweeps outward like a record groove linking to the e. One flat mustard irregular accent behind Less. No music-note stickers, preserve hand-print skeleton.

items.example_title: The Day We Took Our Time
items.lettering_notes: Handlee's light round soft pen handwriting, near-monoline and open. RIGHT title with Day large above, The and We Took tucked naturally around it, Our Time dominant below. Teal main ink, a short terracotta wash behind Time. Enlarge T crossbar into a wide arch; final e has a long unhurried loop that follows the distant road contour. Unequal word sizes, relaxed spacing, no thick calligraphic brush conversion.

Give You Glory's delicate jumping handwritten pen forms, uneven narrow strokes and small loops. RIGHT title: Read Me smaller high, River large with an exaggerated R downstroke, by the tucked in the interline gap. Muted lilac and pale cream over dark water. One long broken r exit forms a low shoreline pen curve; occasional double retraced strokes only at R and M, keep airy handprint rather than ornate brush.

WindSong's very fine high-contrast calligraphic script with extreme hairline turns. Enormous L in Light carries the left title, All the small above its shoulder, We Saved nestled below. Pale-gold and ivory. Stretch the L cross-stroke into a sweeping open luminous-ink arch enclosing just two sides, with one darker ochre echo. Keep hairlines fine, no generic heavy brush or symmetrical frame.

Whisper's light airy connected script with small brush-pressure variation. RIGHT title: One More small high, Ordinary smaller mid, Miracle very large with a tall open M embracing the small middle word. Ivory main ink and sparse muted gold pen-strand echoes. M's exit and final e bend like two gentle piano-phrase arcs, part of lettering, not separate music notes. Long terminals, no thick impasto.

Vujahday Script's relaxed expressive slanted joins and medium-weight pressure changes. LEFT title with huge S in Summer upper, Has tiny, Loose Ends lower shifted right. Deep cobalt ink with a coral alternate contour only on selected loops. The final s gives a wild loose-thread curl wrapping once around the lower word and leaving a deliberate open end. No separate rope graphics, beach objects stay clear.

The Girl Next Door's thin casual diary handwriting, upright loose handwritten print and soft uneven loops. RIGHT title: small Please Leave the high, Window large center, Open still larger below with a giant O. Dusty terracotta ink; a soft faded ochre horizontal paint swath peeks behind Open. W terminal becomes one long wandering pen line toward the curtain, slight retracing on a few corners. Do not convert to ornate wedding script.

Neucha's slim quirky upright hand-print, narrow bowls and blunt irregular stems. LEFT title: Where the small, Wild medium, ROADS giant below and Meet nested at its right. Deep charcoal letters, ROADS partly reversed as unpainted pale sky inside a rough moss-green brush slab. R leg and M stem continue as two diverging thin route strokes, both attached to lettering. Preserve narrow friendly forms, no stencil military font.

Indie Flower's wide wobbly rounded pen-print, almost monoline with childish open counters. RIGHT title: We Found small, a tiny, Softer dominant with extra-large S, World broad low. Forest-green ink and one gentle apricot highlight on the S stem. W and d terminals stretch into long wandering growth lines with two small leaf-shaped ink strokes attached. Bold scale and irregular heights, not connected calligraphy or a separate botanical border.

Crafty Girls' playful thin curling handwritten print and irregular loops. LEFT title with a large S and very large W, Save a Seat arranged in a light rising cluster, for tiny before the lower Wonder. Cream pen with restrained lemon accent. Extend two round letter counters into loose double circles that interlock around word gaps; a few short wavy terminal marks, no stars, crowns or standalone chair icons. Preserve thin quirky strokes.

Fuzzy Bubbles' soft thin rounded hand-print, bubbly counters and short limbs. RIGHT title: Tiny small above, Reasons medium and Stay huge staggered below. Deep sage, warm terracotta and cream selective colors, using distinct letter colors on Stay only. Exaggerate S and y loop; a thin pencil-like second contour trails around just one large counter. One irregular apricot paint patch sits behind the t, no floating circles, keep letters light and playful.

Short Stack's wide rounded compact hand-print, blunt endings and slightly uneven block spacing. LEFT title: Almost small high, Where medium, We tiny nested, BELONG huge low with exaggerated B and G. Cream and muted mustard, a thin rust edge offset on B and O. Short broken color blocks sit behind selected strokes; one G tail gives a broad short double sweep. Keep friendly hand-print, no brush-script conversion or extra hotel text.

Itim's thick friendly rounded upright hand-print and compact counters. RIGHT title: The Good Kind small high, of tiny, LOST huge below, giant L and round O. Gold and cream with an imperfect dark-green cutout in O. L foot forks into a short attached trail-like end. Non-cursive, unequal letter heights.

Calligraffitti's very fine forward-slanted connected pen-script. LEFT title: oversized W of Write; to Me nested beside it, in tiny, November large below. Deep olive with a muted rust echo. The t crossbar and r terminal become an airy open postal-route-like sweep through the interline gap. No stamps or separate badges.

Dr Sugiyama's thick downward brush weight and very thin fast joins. RIGHT title: Chase medium high, the Last tiny below, Orange huge center, Sky lower shifted right. Warm ivory and sunset orange, oversized O and long y. The y descender makes one fierce tapered arc echoing the running track; bristle strands only on O and C.

Delicious Handrawn's relaxed upright quick hand-print and round imperfect bowls. RIGHT title: Keep a Little small high, Weather huge with giant W, Inside broad beneath. Warm cream and marigold. W terminal curves like the awning edge; i dots stretch into short ink rain streaks, sparse doubled retracing on a few letter corners. Not ornate script, no umbrella icons.

Mali's soft rounded open hand-print with gentle near-monoline turns. RIGHT title: Room medium above tiny for Another, Sunrise huge below with wide S and tall final e. Sage ink, loose translucent peach wash behind Sunrise center. Pale-yellow curve attached to S and an open e terminal suggest the sunrise contour. Rounded print, no standalone sun.

Sriracha's rounded forward-leaning medium pen forms, compact joins. LEFT title: Sweetness large high, Takes small under S, Its tiny, Time huge low. Dark forest-green and orange. Dry ochre swipe behind Time allows pale reverse sections in T and i; T bar extends into a slanted citrus-peel-like pen curl, attached to letter. No fruit stickers.

Leckerli One's heavy rounded connected script and bulbous joins. LEFT title: The Days small high, Taste Like nested mid, Honey huge below with big H and long y. Cream and amber-gold. A single attached rounded ink droplet tapers from y; small amber reverse patch under an H stem. No bees or honeycomb badges, keep rounded script.

items.example_title: Leave a Light in the Valley
items.lettering_notes: Norican's heavy slanted brush-script body and smooth thick-thin joins. RIGHT title: Leave a small high, Light large mid, in the tiny nested, Valley huge low with enormous V. Warm-gold and cream strand accents. V descender and y tail sweep into converging arcs following the valley ridges, attached and fully inside frame; no mountain icons.

Oregano's narrow informal slightly leaning hand-print, soft small bowls and modest varied pen weight. RIGHT title: The Wind small high, Forgot mid, Our tiny, Names huge low with tall N. Charcoal and thin coral ghost edges on selected strokes, no repeated words. N diagonal and s exit drag into airy broken wind-lines; no feathers or tag icons.

items.example_title: See You When the Seasons Turn
items.lettering_notes: Meow Script's fine flowing connected calligraphy, lean ascenders and sharp delicate pressure changes. LEFT title: See You medium high, When the tiny between lines, Seasons large and Turn larger offset low. Cream and copper. A huge opening S loops back to embrace two words; final n makes a long open sweep with exactly two attached small leaf-shaped ink strokes. No thick generic brush or symmetric wreath.
